blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Employer branding has been one of the biggest shifts in HR over the last decade. In the past, companies only cared about how they looked to customers. Today, the way you look to candidates is just as important.

A strong employer brand is not a marketing trick. It is a truthful story about what it is really like to work at the company — supported by the experiences of current employees on platforms like Glassdoor, LinkedIn and social media. Companies have been investing heavily in employee stories, career pages, and transparent communication about culture and values.

When reality matches the story, the brand grows. When it doesn't, candidates quickly notice. That is why authenticity, rather than a clever slogan, is now the real test of an employer brand.

items.q: According to the text, how has HR changed over the last decade?
options: Companies have stopped caring about customers
Companies now care about how they look to candidates, not only to customers
HR has become less important than marketing
Companies now advertise only on television
items.why: "the way you look to candidates is just as important" — antes só importava a imagem para o cliente.

items.q: What does the text say a strong employer brand really is?
options: A truthful story about what it is like to work at the company
items.why: "It is a truthful story about what it is really like to work at the company."

items.q: What have companies been investing in, according to the text?
options: Employee stories, career pages and transparent communication
items.why: "investing heavily in employee stories, career pages, and transparent communication."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Current employees' experiences shape the employer brand
A great slogan can hide a poor workplace from candidates
Authenticity matters more than clever wording
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que os candidatos percebem rápido quando a realidade não bate — um slogan não esconde nada.

items.q: The last paragraph suggests that an employer brand fails when…
options: the internal reality does not match the story it tells
the company spends too little on advertising
items.why: Inferência: "When it doesn't, candidates quickly notice" — a marca cresce só quando a realidade confirma a história.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conversando com o time de marketing sobre a nova página de carreiras. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, so before we design a single screen, let's be clear about what this careers page is for. It has to feel like us — not like a brochure. If it reads like an advert, candidates will stop trusting it in about ten seconds.

I've been talking to people across the teams, and the strongest material we have is real. One analyst told me about the mentoring she got in her first year. Someone in operations described how a mistake was handled with support, not blame. That is the story we want on the page — honest, specific, human.

So here is what I'd like from marketing. Instead of writing testimonials for people, let's record them in their own words and lightly edit. Photos of the actual teams, not stock images. And we link straight to our Glassdoor profile — yes, including the reviews we cannot control.

I know that feels risky. But if the good stories are genuine, the page will do the work for us. The moment it looks polished and fake, we lose the exact candidates we're trying to attract.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily want the careers page to feel like?
options: A ranking of the best employees
The company itself — honest and human
items.why: "It has to feel like us — not like a brochure… honest, specific, human."

items.q: What examples does Emily give of strong, real material?
options: Mentoring in an analyst's first year and a mistake handled with support
items.why: "the mentoring she got… a mistake was handled with support, not blame."

items.q: What does Emily ask marketing to do with the testimonials?
options: Write them on behalf of the employees
Record them in the employees' own words and lightly edit
items.why: "Instead of writing testimonials for people, let's record them in their own words and lightly edit."

items.q: Why is Emily willing to link to the Glassdoor reviews the company cannot control?
options: Because genuine stories build trust, even with some negative reviews
Because the reviews are all positive
items.why: Inferência: ela aceita o risco porque a autenticidade — inclusive das críticas — é o que gera confiança.

items.q: What is Emily most worried about?
options: That competitors will copy the page
That the page will cost too much to build
That the page will look polished and fake, driving away the right candidates
That employees will refuse to appear
items.why: "The moment it looks polished and fake, we lose the exact candidates we're trying to attract."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Our employer brand is how people picture working here before they even apply." An employer brand is…
options: the reputation the company has as a place to work
the salary offered to new hires
items.why: Employer brand = marca empregadora: como a empresa é vista como lugar para trabalhar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "A clear ___ tells candidates exactly what makes this company unique to work for."
items.why: Value proposition = proposta de valor: o que torna a empresa única para o candidato.

items.q: "We want to showcase real employee stories on the page." To showcase means to…
options: display in a positive, prominent way
items.why: To showcase = destacar / exibir de forma favorável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Being ___ about pay and culture builds more trust than a polished slogan."
items.why: Transparent = transparente: comunicação aberta e honesta gera confiança.

items.q: Authenticity is best described as…
options: the number of applicants a company receives
the internal experience matching the external message
items.why: Authenticity = autenticidade: a experiência real por dentro bate com a mensagem por fora.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de RH e marketing sobre marca empregadora. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "HR still has to sign off on the new careers page before launch." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the employee stories one department at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "A strong brand helps us stand out from other employers." To stand out means to…
items.why: Stand out = destacar-se, ser notado em meio aos demais.

items.q: "If the reality doesn't match the message, candidates will quickly see through it." To see through something means to…
options: read it carefully to the end
items.why: See through = enxergar a falsidade, perceber que algo é falso.

items.q: "Honest testimonials really move the needle on our cost-per-hire." This means they…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
